correctness.rationale: For symmetric K-category Dirichlet shape a>0, beta-binomial marginal and two-category factorial moments give Cov(M1,M2)=K² p1 p2[R(a)−1] with a positive prefactor. The exact rising-factorial ratio R is reconstructed by cancelling labeled singleton and doubleton count probabilities. With t=1/a, it factors into an increasing product of (1−1/(K−1+jt)^2) and rational factor B(t). Its log derivative has cubic numerator c0+c1t+c2t²+c3t³; for n≥4 and K≥2+binom(n−1,2), substitution v=n−4 in the four coefficients yields explicit strictly positive polynomials and derivatives, proving strict monotonicity all t≥0. Endpoints give R(t=0)<1 and R(t→∞)>1 precisely for K≥K0, proving unique sign change as a increases. Independent exact multinomial count-vector enumeration for n=4,K=5 at four rational shapes confirms the ratios and + to − covariance; symbolic derivative identities checked on a bounded n,K grid, not mistaken for the universal polynomial proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the complete single-crossing covariance theorem for occupancy singleton versus doubleton classes and its sharp large-alphabet sufficient cutoff. General Dirichlet-multinomial moment formulas are standard and not new. Mao–Ma study Dirichlet-tree mixtures for microbiome compositional data; Zhu studies the marginal law of number of distinct sampled types, not a covariance between M1 and M2 across concentration values. Resultary published uniform occupancy one-switch law concerns observed richness against an r-frequency count with iid uniform probabilities; it is not this Dirichlet mixture singleton-doubleton covariance. Exact equivalent theorem could occur in specialized Bayesian species-sampling and frequency-spectrum literature.
residual_risks: The all-a single-crossing claim may appear under frequency-spectrum/occupancy aliases in specialized species sampling literature.
The cutoff is for strict small-a endpoint ratio only; no phase diagram for K<K0 is claimed.
